beats.say: Every data engineering loop has a SQL round.
Senior candidates do not fail on syntax. They fail on edge cases.
beats.label: Where points are lost
beats.head: Edge cases, not syntax

beats.say: Three skills cover most rounds: window functions, deduplication, and reading a plan.
beats.label: Track 3 · SQL for senior loops

check.prompt: Two rows tie for second place. Which function leaves a gap after them?

beats.say: First: window functions.
A window function looks at other rows, but keeps every row. Group by would collapse them.
beats.label: The idea
beats.head: Look at other rows, keep every row

beats.say: Row number gives one, two, three. Rank leaves gaps after a tie. Dense rank leaves no gaps.
beats.label: Three ranking functions

beats.say: The trap is ties. Always say what happens when two rows have the same value.
beats.label: Interview trap
beats.head: What about ties?

check.prompt: Your dedupe query gives a different row on each run. What is missing?
check.why: When two rows share the same time, the order is not fixed. A tie-breaker makes it deterministic.

beats.say: Second: keep one row per key.
Number the rows inside each key, newest first. Then keep row number one.
beats.label: The pattern
beats.text: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY updated_at DESC)

beats.say: But if two rows share the same time, the result can change on every run.
beats.label: The trap
beats.head: Same time, random winner

beats.say: So add a tie-breaker to the order. Now the query is deterministic.
beats.label: The fix
beats.head: Add a tie-breaker

beats.say: Third: streaks and sessions.
A user logs in five days in a row. How do you find that streak?
beats.label: The question
beats.head: Find a streak of days

beats.say: Subtract the row number from the date. Rows in one streak get the same result.
beats.label: The trick
beats.head: Date minus row number

beats.say: Last: why is the query slow?
Do not guess. Read the plan. Find the step that takes the most time.
beats.label: Step one
beats.head: Read the plan

beats.say: Filter on the partition column. Select fewer columns. And watch for joins that multiply rows.
beats.label: Common fixes

beats.say: Quick recap of SQL for senior loops.
Windows keep rows. Dedupe with a tie-breaker. And read the plan before you tune.
beats.label: SQL for senior loops

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
